summary:
## Project Overview
This tutorial guides you through sewing the **Danielle Jacket**, a chic twill jacket featuring contrast binding, patch pockets, and a full lining. You will learn the complete construction process from assembling the main body to adding the final buttons.

## Required Materials
*   Danielle Jacket sewing pattern
*   Main fabric (e.g., twill)
*   Lining fabric
*   5 **buttons**
*   1 cm wide pre-folded **binding tape**

## Construction Steps

### Main Jacket Assembly
1.  **Sew Body**: With right sides together, sew the **front panels** to the **back panel** at the shoulders and side seams.
2.  **Sew Sleeves**: Fold each **sleeve** with right sides together and sew the inseam.
3.  **Set Sleeves**: With the jacket wrong side out and sleeves right side out, insert the sleeves into the armholes. Pin and sew, ensuring the underarm seams match up.

### Pockets
1.  **Bind Top Edge**: Apply binding to the top edge of both pocket pieces first.
2.  **Position Pockets**: Place the pockets on the front panels.

    > [!NOTE]
    > **Pocket Placement**: Position pockets **10 cm** up from the hem and **8 cm** from the center front.

3.  **Attach Pockets**: Fold the side and bottom seam allowances under and stitch the pockets to the jacket. The topstitching on the bound edge is completed later with matching thread.

### Lining Assembly
*   Follow the same assembly steps as the main jacket for the lining body and sleeves.

    > [!IMPORTANT]
    > Remember to **trim 1 cm off the hem** of the lining sleeves. This ensures the lining sits correctly inside the main sleeve without peeking out.

### Joining Lining & Finishing Sleeves
1.  With the main jacket right side out and lining wrong side out, insert the lining into the jacket.
2.  Pull the main sleeve and lining sleeve through the jacket body, right sides together, and **sew the sleeve hems together**.
3.  Turn the sleeves right side out. The lining should start 1 cm from the edge of the main sleeve. Press the sleeve hems.

### Binding & Final Assembly
1.  **Pin Lining**: Smooth the lining inside the jacket and pin it along the front opening and neckline, aligning all seams.
2.  **Sew Neckline**: Sew the lining to the jacket at the neckline.
3.  **Apply Binding**: Apply the pre-folded binding tape around the entire jacket opening (hem, front edges, and neckline).

    > [!TIP]
    > For neat corners, **fold the binding** instead of cutting it. Start and end your binding at a side seam to make the join less visible. Always use thread that matches your binding tape.

4.  **Finish Pockets**: With the binding thread still in the machine, topstitch the top edge of the pockets.

### Buttons & Buttonholes
1.  **Mark Buttonholes**: Mark buttonhole placement on one side of the front opening.
2.  **Mark Buttons**: Mark corresponding button placement on the other side.

    > [!NOTE]
    > **Button Spacing**:
    > *   First button: **4 cm** from the neckline.
    > *   Next buttons: **12 cm** apart.
    > *   Last button: **11 cm** from the previous one.

3.  **Sew**: Create the buttonholes and sew on the buttons. It's recommended to practice on a scrap piece of fabric first.
transcription:
## Introduction & Required Materials

Hi and welcome to yet another tutorial. My name is Karolina and in this tutorial, I'll show you how to make this cute Jacket using my new sewing pattern called Danielle. You can buy this pattern from my shop on Etsy and I'll leave a link in the description, if you want to check it out.

You'll need a cut-out pieces in main fabric and lining, as well as five buttons and one centimeter wide pre-folded binding tape for this project.

## Assembling the Main Jacket Body & Sleeves

To start, lay the back panel on the right side and pin the front panels, right side to right side on the shoulders and sides.

Then fold the sleeve right side to right side and sew the inside seam together.

With the jacket on the wrong side and sleeves on the right side, insert the sleeves into the jacket and pin the armholes together. Start from the underarm seam so they match up and continue to pin the rest of the armhole and repeat the same steps on the other sleeve.

## Creating & Attaching the Pockets

Bind the top edge of the pockets. Of course you'll need to use a matching thread to the color of your binding.

Place pockets on the front panels 10 centimeters up from the hem and 8 centimeters from the center front. Pin the pocket to ensure that it stays in place. Then fold the seam allowance of the pocket inside starting from the sides, then the bottom, and on the end the corners.

Measure both pockets to make sure that they're even.

Then stitch the pockets to the jacket. As we are using beige thread start topstitching the pocket after the binding. We'll finish the pockets next time we have a black thread on the machine.

## Assembling the Jacket Lining

Moving on to the lining, you want to repeat the same steps as we did with the jacket. Sew together back and front panels on the shoulders and side seams, right side to right side.

Fold sleeves in half and sew the inside seam together. I forgot to record to trim one centimeter of the hem of the sleeve, so just remember to do so as lining for the sleeve should be a bit shorter than the main fabric sleeve.

With lining jacket on the wrong side and sleeves on the right side, insert the sleeves into the jacket and pin the armholes.

## Attaching the Lining to the Sleeves

Place jacket on the right side and turn sleeves to the wrong side. Make sure that they are not twisted.

Now with lining jacket on the wrong side, fold the sleeve by a bit and then, insert it to the sleeve of the main jacket.

Repeat the same steps with the second sleeve hem and sew them together.

Then turn the sleeves to the right side.

Lay out lining inside nicely and then pin sleeves, so the lining starts one centimeter from the end of the sleeve. That's why we needed to trim off one centimeter of the hem of the lining sleeves before. And then press the sleeve using an iron, so it stays in place.

## Finishing the Neckline & Edges with Binding

Moving on, pin the lining to the jacket. Make sure that all the seams are nicely aligned together.

Now that everything is pinned down, sew the neckline together.

Then trim off seam allowance, but be careful not to cut the stitch line.

Next, we need to bind the opening.

Instead of cutting binding on each corner, fold the binding and continue to stitch down. This way you will get a much nicer finish.

Start binding from the side seams, so the joined end of the binding is not very visible. Make sure to take your time on doing this, and don't rush. Also I think it goes without saying that you need to change the thread to match the color of your binding.

Once you get to the end cut the binding and fold the end by a bit for a smooth finish.

## Adding Buttons & Final Details

Then topstitch the binding bit on the pockets we left, while we have some same color thread.

Mark the placement of the buttons on the right side of the jacket. First button should be 4 centimeters from the neckline. Then each next one 12 centimeters apart and the last button should be 11 centimeters away. Mark position of the buttonholes on the other side with the same measurements as for buttons. I would highly recommend to make a test of the buttonhole first.

Then open the buttonholes using an unpicker and sew the buttons to the jacket.

Also if you want, you can add buttons to the pockets or to the cuffs.

And that's it. Your own perfect Danielle Jacket. Thanks for watching!

## Final Look

_A final look at the finished Danielle Jacket._
